_meta.indication: Treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults to reduce cardiovascular mortality and cardiovascular-related hospitalization.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (the sole trial establishing efficacy)
pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:2:2 to tafamidis 20 mg, tafamidis 80 mg, or placebo once daily for 30 months in addition to standard of care, stratified by TTR genotype and baseline NYHA class.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with wild-type or hereditary transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and NYHA Class I-III symptoms.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was a hierarchical (Finkelstein-Schoenfeld) combined analysis of all-cause mortality and rate of cardiovascular-related hospitalization over 30 months (pooled tafamidis vs. placebo).
pivotal_trials.n: N=441 (tafamidis 20 mg n=88, tafamidis 80 mg n=176, placebo n=177)
pivotal_trials.result: Significant reduction (p=0.0006) in the combined primary endpoint for pooled VYNDAQEL vs placebo; all-cause mortality hazard ratio 0.70 (95% CI 0.51, 0.96; p=0.026), a 30% relative reduction in risk of death; more patients alive at Month 30 (186 [70.5%] vs 101 [57.1%]) with fewer CV-related hospitalizations (0.297 vs 0.455 per patient per year).

key_safety: The frequency of adverse events with tafamidis was similar to placebo; adverse-event-related discontinuations were similar between groups (80-mg 12 [7%], 20-mg 5 [6%], placebo 11 [6%]). Several events of special interest (diarrhea, urinary tract infection) occurred less frequently on tafamidis than placebo.
target_moa: Tafamidis is a transthyretin (TTR) stabilizer; it binds to one of the thyroxine (T4) binding sites on the TTR tetramer, stabilizing the tetramer and preventing its dissociation into monomers, which reduces amyloid formation and deposition.
modality: Small molecule (orally administered tafamidis/tafamidis meglumine capsule)

advisory_committee.vote: The applications were not referred to an FDA advisory committee because they did not raise significant public health questions and clearly provided substantial evidence of effectiveness with no critical safety issues.
